name: Helmet
role: head: the centurion helmet with its transverse crest
what_i_did: Imperial Gallic helmet built as named parts: bowl, brow band and rib, visor, neck guard, hinged cheek guards wrapped round the face, ear guards, bowl studs, and a crest of 8 blocks on a holder and post. Faceted with a light Voronoi displace so it reads like the concept's cut-paper planes.
good: The crest, bowl, brow band, studs and visor all line up with the concept; the crest arch is the strongest match.
Every piece is its own named mesh, so the crest or cheek guards can be swapped or recoloured on their own.
3,550 triangles, cheap enough for every soldier on screen.
off: Outline match 0.76. The cheek guards are flatter slabs than the concept's folded, angled plates, and the neck guard flares out further to the back.
The concept is a three-quarter view; the score camera is the best-matching side view found by search, so the number is a guide.
The concept's ear guards are small curls; here they are simple tabs.
creative_additions: Bronze-free: the whole helmet stays ivory, as the concept is monochrome; the stud rows are kept as separate pieces so a later bronze trim is one material swap.

rounds.t: First build: bowl, brow band, visor, neck guard, cheek guards, crest of 8 blocks.
Cheek guards wrapped round the face and flared; ear guards and studs added; crest raised on a holder and post.
Facet pass (0.007) for the paper-cut look; camera search; final 768 px / 48 sample render.

score.method: silhouette IoU after bounding-box normalising both masks; camera found by grid search on the model, so a guide
